summary: Midday throughput cliff on dedicated capacity traced to silent-tenant heartbeat suppression causing allocator queue blocking and autoscaler stall
description:
Issue summary:
During a midday traffic window (approx 12:45–13:15 UTC) a FinNova dedicated capacity cluster experienced a sharp drop in successful throughput for batched routes serving redwood-rlhf-13b. P50 remained acceptable but p95/p99 spiked and many requests were queued >10s. Customers reported timeouts and increased 5xx rate.

Impact:
- FinNova observed ~40% throughput loss for critical batching routes for ~24 minutes.
- Several requests hit route-level timeouts and triggered client retries.
- No billing or data-loss impact observed.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: finnova-prod-1 (reserved)
- Region: us-east-1
- Models: redwood-rlhf-13b (pinned v2026-02-28), fallback to open-llama-13b-v2 enabled

Steps to reproduce (as observed):
1) Targeted load pattern: many small interactive streams (~200–300 simultaneous short streams) started after a quiet period.
2) Autoscaler did not provision additional GPU attachments in expected window; allocator queue showed a buildup.
3) Inflight attach requests were blocked behind a set of hung leases where heartbeats from a low-traffic tenant were being suppressed (no obvious CPU/GPU saturation).

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler metrics showed low demand signal preceding the incident, then a sudden spike; autoscaler decision loop returned "no-scale" for several evaluation cycles due to stale telemetry from allocator.
- Allocator queue length increased; the first-in-line attachments remained pending because a small group of sockets associated with a quiet tenant had suppressed heartbeats and held ephemeral slot reservations.
- Prefetch and batching subsystems could not drain; per-gpu slot usage reported a small number of slots at >99% reservation while overall utilization stayed moderate.

Expected behavior:
- Allocator should time out suppressed heartbeats/leases quickly and allow new attachments to use slots.
- Autoscaler should react to sudden spike by scaling up a minimal number of GPUs or triggering fallback routing to lower-cost variants before p99 latency increases.

Logs / dashboards referenced:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/fin-nova/dedicated-pool-overview?var=pool=finnova-prod-1
- Allocator trace: traces.redwood.local/alloc/500321 (internal link)
- Slack thread: #support-finnova (ts 2026-03-10 12:56 UTC)
- Related incident on status page: INC-2026-0310-01

Initial hypothesis:
- A silent/quiet tenant with sporadic long-lived socket sessions suppressed heartbeats from sidecar, holding ephemeral slot reservations. This caused a head-of-line blocking in the allocator queue. Autoscaler inputs were skewed by delayed telemetry and did not scale in time. Noise was not the typical CPU/GPU saturation signal but reservation-level interference (noisy-neighbor-like).
comments: 2026-03-10 13:05 - Priya Shah (Support): A customer reported timeouts and high p99 — triage started. Assigned to Mateo. Opened allocator trace and initial timeline.

2026-03-10 13:18 - Mateo Alvarez (SRE): Observed allocator queue growth and several ATTACH operations in 'waiting' state for >9s. Noted suppressed heartbeats on tenant T-1849 sockets. Added observability hooks to capture sidecar heartbeat metrics.

2026-03-10 13:34 - Eng on-call (Ibrahim): Confirmed autoscaler saw low moving-average due to delayed attach completions; filed a short-term mitigation to lower autoscale evaluation window to 10s for the pool as an emergency step.

2026-03-10 14:02 - Mateo Alvarez (SRE): Temporary mitigation applied: reduced allocator lease timeout to 6s for pool finnova-prod-1 and restarted allocator workers on 3 nodes. Throughput recovered to baseline at ~13:10 UTC.
2026-03-12 09:20 - Product Ops (Zoe Chen): Post-incident follow-up: customer notified, incident summary prepared, planned follow-ups added to backlog.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 13:10 - Correlated p99 spike with allocator queue length metric (alloc.queue_length jumped from 2 to 47).

2026-03-10 13:12 - Captured sidecar heartbeat stats: tenant T-1849 had websocket groups with heartbeat delta > 45s while usual delta < 1s. Sockets showed no CPU/GPU attach errors — held ephemeral slot reservations in 'reserved' state.
2026-03-10 13:16 - Autoscaler logs: evaluation loop ignored spike due to smoothing parameter (ema window 300s). Autoscaler recommended values were suppressed by stale attach completion counts.

2026-03-10 13:20 - Ran targeted attach cancellation on hung reservations (internal command: allocatorctl cancel-hung --pool finnova-prod-1 --tenant T-1849 --age>8s). This freed 8 slots and allowed backlog to drain.

2026-03-10 13:30 - Applied emergency config change: allocator.lease_timeout reduced from 20s -> 6s (pool-scope). Autoscale smoothing window reduced from 300s -> 10s for finnova-prod-1. Observed steady recovery to normal throughput over next 8 minutes.

2026-03-11 11:00 - Reproduced locally with load replay harness: simulate quiet-period long-lived sockets + bursty small streams. Verified allocator queue head-of-line lock when heartbeats are suppressed at sidecar level. Added unit tests and an integration harness.
resolution: Workaround and fix applied: emergency mitigation (shorter lease timeout + smaller autoscale window) restored throughput within 10 minutes. Root fix implemented in allocator to detect suppressed heartbeat patterns and proactively expire ephemeral reservations; autoscaler smoothing logic updated to use burst detection heuristics for dedicated pools. Patch deployed to canary on 2026-03-11 and rolled to the affected pool on 2026-03-12. Customer notified and credits applied for impacted window.
root_cause: Allocator allowed ephemeral slot reservations to persist when sidecar heartbeats were suppressed for a low-traffic tenant. This created head-of-line blocking in the allocator queue. Autoscaler's long smoothing window masked the sudden spike, preventing timely scale-up. Combined effect resembled a noisy-neighbor allocation interference despite overall moderate GPU utilization.
action_items: AUT-1: Add a heartbeat-anomaly detector in allocator to surface tenants with suppressed heartbeat deltas (owner: allocator-team, ETA: 2026-03-24)
AUT-2: Introduce a pool-scoped emergency autoscale mode that bypasses long EMA smoothing when alloc queue length exceeds threshold (owner: autoscaler-team, ETA: 2026-03-20)
AUT-3: Hardening: ensure allocatorctl can safely and automatically expire 'reserved' ephemeral leases older than configured threshold and emit audit logs (owner: infra-ops, ETA: 2026-03-18)
AUT-4: Run a chaos test scenario simulating quiet-tenant heartbeat suppression and bursty small streams as part of weekly dedicated pool resilience tests (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-04-01)
AUT-5: Follow-up with FinNova CS: technical summary and recommended client-side best practices for long-lived connections (owner: Support, ETA: 2026-03-13)
